headline: Repeat-resolved human genome analysis links transposable elements to chromatin states
label: Repeat Element Genome Architecture
summary: Complete T2T human genomes now allow repeat annotation to be paired with epigenomic readout, alongside new tools for repeat detection and genotyping.
synthesis: The dominant thread is analysis of repeat-rich sequence in complete or near-complete genomes, with repeat detection paired to other readouts where relevant. A telomere-to-telomere study profiles 3.7 million transposable elements across 12 human cell lines with multi-modal epigenomic data, reporting H3K9me3 evasion and CTCF invasion as features of a host-TE evolutionary arms race. FuzzyClusTeR provides a web server detecting tandem and diffuse repeat clusters, applied to telomeric-like repeats in T2T-CHM13v2.0 with simulation. STRmie-HD performs alignment-free, interruption-aware HTT CAG/CCG genotyping and somatic mosaicism profiling across Illumina, PacBio, and Nanopore. The structure-led metagenome search for RNA-guided nucleases is methodologically adjacent rather than repeat-focused. What is new is pairing repeat annotation with epigenomic state in a complete human reference. All four items are preprints, and their connection is interpretive rather than a shared experimental design.
